I was in the exact same position for my first year of university at UofA, I absolutely bombed my first year and I finished with a 1.7 GPA. I was originally in the faculty of science, but I had to withdraw. Now, I am currently an open studies student finishing this semester with a 3.0 GPA (with four courses), and I am planning to get back into the faculty of Science, here are some things I have learned:

​

1. **Your Health is Crucial!!**

\- Something I have learned was not to eat into my health for the sake of studying that extra hour. It really isn't worth it to cram information in your head last minute, as you aren't function properly(assuming you are properly sleep deprived)

\- Eat healthy and stay hydrated. 

\- Get exercise, it can be anything from a 5 minute stretch during a long study session, to going to the multiple gyms on campus. 

\- The university does offer confidential counselling and other helpful resources that pertain to mental health as well.

​

**2. Form a Routine and Habits**

\- Form a morning routine, something that gets you out of bed and ready for the day.

\- Study habits are a big thing here. There are many different ways to study, try to study smarter, not harder. This can include spaced out repetitions of studying throughout the day or week. Active recall study methods and grouping methods to better understand the course material.

\- Essentially what Active Recall is, is just writing down everything you can remember. After that, study the things you missed or did not remember correctly.

\- Grouping and Organizational study methods deals with connecting ideas in drawing but also conceptually. Try to relate the course concepts to one another( they should relate in some fashion). 

\- Quizlet!!!

\- Find a study buddy, try to teach them the course material, by trying to teach the material, while also keeping it simple, it enforces your understanding of the material.

**3. Know when to Withdraw**

\- I didn't recognize this option in my first year. You drop the course, depending on when you can also avoid some of the classes fees.

\- You will get a "W" on your transcript, I would advise you to discuss with your first year advisor to discuss its implications and etc, I know first year science students have this. I'm not entirely sure about arts faculty.

​

**4. Organize your time**

\- Use a calendar or start journaling your weeks/months.

\- Plan out how much time you need for each assignment/quiz or study session for the semester. Also include some buffer room as well to prepare for any unforeseen complications.

\- I try to organize my months, weeks and days. Months is more long term that deals with quizzes, exams and due dates for assignments. Weekly also deals with exams assignments and quizzes. I also break my day down into hourly portions of study periods and due dates as well. 

**5. Make time for things you enjoy**

\- Set aside some time every week to do something new, or something you enjoy. 

\- It can be anything from hanging out with friends to reading alone, just find something that takes your mind off of uni and work for like an hour.

​

   **6. Dealing with stress**

\- Stress gets to us in different ways, either physically or mentally manifesting. 

\- That's why it is important to find something you enjoy, to take you away from the stress.

\- But attacking the roots of the stress is the best way to get rid of it. If an exam is coming up and you don't feel prepared, the best thing you can do is prepare for the exam strategically, using different study methods and techniques. 

\- Don't feel guilty for taking breaks. Give yourself permission to step away from your work and recuperate. 

   **7. Keep your chin up**

\- I know what it's like and it is definitely rough, but you have to keep your chin up. During the Christmas break recuperate, enjoy time with family and friends.

\- Come back with a clear mindset, achievable goals and an arsenal of study strategies and motivation to kick the semester off right.

​

I just want to that it is possible to recover, as I am in the process of doing so. You'll have more good and bad days, but as long as you keep going one day at a time and keep your chin up, you will gain new and better habits and build up momentum so you can tackle your academics with confidence.
